lead_headline: Saturday freeze ends the week: Restaurant tracker logs sixth consecutive day with zero new leads as May closes with detection machinery fully dormant

restaurant.blurb: Sixth straight day without new leads—detection silence extends through Saturday as May closes with complete vacancy. Active pipeline frozen at 188 leads (106 openings, 82 closures).

liquor.blurb: Day 31: May closes with complete regulatory blackout—Colorado's liquor licensing system enters June having posted zero applications, zero status changes, zero administrative activity for entire 31-day month. All 12,396 tracked licenses remain frozen as Memorial Day weekend concludes the most comprehensive licensing shutdown since tracking began. The May paralysis sets historic record—first full calendar month with absolute zero activity across all categories, all counties, all license types. State authorities maintain complete silence on restoration timeline while invisible application backlog presumably compounds through month's end. June opens Monday with no signals of resumed operations as licensing apparatus enters second month with unknown restart date.

reputation.blurb: 45 mentions this week across 9 sources—week closes down 29% from prior week's 63 as Memorial Day suppression fully manifests. Denver Post leads with 13 citations (29%), Instagram contributes 11, Facebook adds 10, Reddit delivers 4. Notable pickups include Greenwood Village office-to-residential incentives (Cherry Creek News) and Broncos' Burnham Yard purchase finalization hitting social channels. Google News RSS exclusively drives all discovery (100% weekly flow). The sustained week-over-week decline confirms extended post-holiday drag on media velocity, though May's monthly total holds at 219 mentions as the month concludes with citation activity 28% below normal pace.

subscriptions.blurb: Net −1 yesterday (0 new, 1 canceled)—sixth consecutive day of zero-or-negative movement as Memorial Day week ends with complete stall. MTD net advances to +31 (+1.0/day), 90-day net stands at +135. The seven-day window shows net +8 (14 new, 6 canceled), salvaging modest weekly gains despite weekend's double-negative finish. Recent pattern reveals sharp divergence: May 18-25 posted only net −1 across eight days, then May 26-28 surged with +9 in three days before Friday-Saturday pullback erased the momentum. YTD pace of +1.3/day continues outperforming MTD rate, but daily flow remains volatile—oscillating between multi-day zero stretches and concentrated acquisition bursts. May closes with trajectory uncertain as brief late-month revival abruptly stalls heading into June.
